Separate algebraic and continuous time on the dyadic solenoid

Skills: formal-thinking-and-answer; sshx. Actual Codex CLI implementation; caller integration and evidence verification. Pro mathematical advice only. Independent validation follows before publication; no model-diverse verification or literature novelty claim.

On the actual dyadic subgroup of Nat -> AddCircle(1), construct a compact connected abelian group with a dense continuous real flow, surjective multiplication in every positive degree, no two-torsion, and an explicit nonzero three-torsion point h. There is a genuine algebraic rational-time homomorphism sending 1 to h; every such map sends (1/4)^n to h and is discontinuous for the usual rational topology. No continuous real-time homomorphism sends 1 to h.

The proof builds the inherited compact topology, matches finite coordinates to prove dense real flow and connectedness, derives all positive roots from compact closed images containing that flow, extends the cyclic rational data by divisibility/Baer, then proves the universal quarter-sequence obstruction. One public theorem; consumed private proof helpers. Classical solenoid background: R. N. Gumerov, arXiv math/0312288v1, Propositions 1 and 2; no novelty claim.

+# Algebraic and Continuous Time in the Dyadic Solenoid
+
+## Abstract
+
+The compact connected dyadic solenoid admits algebraic rational time at a nonzero order-three point, but no continuous rational or real time there.
+
+Let S2 be the additive subgroup of the product of unit additive circles consisting of sequences x with 2 times x(n+1) equal to x(n). Its topology is the subspace topology of that product. This is the dyadic carrier, distinct from the all-positive-degree UniversalSolenoid: only doubling compatibility is imposed here, and S2 has a nonzero point h with coordinates (-1)^n/3 modulo one.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (A divisible compact connected group separates algebraic and continuous time).**
+
+$$\operatorname{Compact}\left(S2\right) \land \left(\operatorname{Connected}\left(S2\right) \land \left(\operatorname{Continuous}\left(j\right) \land \left(\operatorname{DenseRange}\left(j\right) \land \left(\left(\forall m \in N,\; 0 < m \Rightarrow \operatorname{Surjective}\left(\operatorname{multiplication}\left(m, S2\right)\right)\right) \land \left(\left(\forall x \in S2,\; 2 \cdot x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\right) \land \left(\neg(h = 0) \land \left(3 \cdot h = 0 \land \left(\left(\exists phi \in \operatorname{AddHom}\left(Q, S2\right),\; \operatorname{phi}\left(1\right) = h\right) \land \left(\left(\forall theta \in \operatorname{AddHom}\left(Q, S2\right),\; \operatorname{theta}\left(1\right) = h \Rightarrow \left(\left(\forall n \in N,\; \operatorname{theta}\left(\frac{1}{4}^{n}\right) = h\right) \land \neg(\operatorname{Continuous}\left(theta\right))\right)\right) \land \neg(\exists psi \in \operatorname{AddHom}\left(R, S2\right),\; \operatorname{Continuous}\left(psi\right) \land \operatorname{psi}\left(1\right) = h)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)\right)$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Solenoid/DyadicTimeSeparation.dyadic_time_separation` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+S2 is a compact connected abelian topological group. For every positive integer m, multiplication by m is surjective. Multiplication by two has zero kernel. The point h is nonzero and 3 times h is zero. There exists an additive homomorphism phi from the rational numbers to S2 with phi(1)=h. Every such homomorphism satisfies phi((1/4)^n)=h for every natural n and is discontinuous for the usual rational topology. There is no continuous additive homomorphism psi from the real numbers to S2 with psi(1)=h.
+
+The map j from the real line has coordinate j(t)(n)=t/2^n modulo one. It is a continuous additive homomorphism with dense image. For a finite set of coordinates choose its largest index N, lift x(N) to a real representative r, and take t=2^N r. Compatibility matches every earlier coordinate exactly. The compatibility equations are closed equalizers in a compact product, proving compactness; the dense continuous image of the connected real line proves connectedness. The image of multiplication by a positive m is compact and closed. It contains j of the real line because t/m is a real preimage, so density makes multiplication surjective.
+
+Compatibility also shows that a point killed by doubling has every coordinate zero. At the alternating third-period point, doubling negates each coordinate and tripling kills it. Divisibility makes the underlying abelian group injective as an integer module. Baer's extension property extends the homomorphism from the integers sending 1 to h along the inclusion of the integers into the rationals. This constructs a genuine additive rational homomorphism without imposing continuity.
+
+Doubling is injective, hence so is multiplication by four, and 4h=h. For any rational homomorphism anchored at h, the recurrence 4 phi((1/4)^(n+1))=phi((1/4)^n) therefore forces every value to equal h. The arguments tend to zero in the usual rational topology, while the image remains the nonzero constant h, contradicting continuity and Hausdorff uniqueness of limits. Restricting a continuous real homomorphism along the continuous rational inclusion gives the real-time obstruction. For the discrete topology on the rational domain every map is continuous; the obstruction concerns its usual topology. The dense real flow j exists, but cannot take the value h at time 1.
+
+These are classical solenoid phenomena. R. N. Gumerov, On finite-sheeted covering mappings onto solenoids, arXiv:math/0312288v1, defines the dyadic case by constant bonding degree two. Propositions 1 and 2 discuss surjective power maps and the homeomorphism property for primes repeated infinitely in the bonding sequence. That multiplicative-circle account provides classical context; the assertions here are proved directly on the displayed additive-circle carrier, without asserting a formally verified identification of the two models or a new result in the literature.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S1/Solenoid/DyadicTimeSeparation.dyadic_time_separation`

+/- GID: D5/S1/Solenoid/DyadicTimeSeparation
+   generality: I
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S1/Solenoid/DyadicTimeSeparation
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:evidence-not-specified-by-formal-manifest)
+   anchors: []
+   utility: none
+   digest: The dyadic solenoid separates algebraic rational time from continuous time. -/
+
+import Mathlib.Topology.Instances.AddCircle.Real
+import Mathlib.Topology.Connected.Basic
+import Mathlib.Topology.Algebra.Group.Basic
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Category.Grp.Injective
+import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic
+
+/-! The dyadic inverse limit and its torsion point separate algebraic and continuous time. -/
+
+noncomputable section
+
+namespace D5.S1.Solenoid
+
+/-- Compatible circle coordinates under doubling. The topology is inherited from the product. -/
+def dyadicSubgroup : AddSubgroup (ℕ → AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) where
+  carrier := {x | ∀ n, 2 • x (n + 1) = x n}
+  zero_mem' := by simp
+  add_mem' := by intro x y hx hy n; simp only [Pi.add_apply, nsmul_add, hx n, hy n]
+  neg_mem' := by intro x hx n; simpa using congrArg Neg.neg (hx n)
+
+abbrev DyadicSolenoid := dyadicSubgroup
+
+namespace DyadicSolenoid
+
+private theorem closed_carrier : IsClosed (dyadicSubgroup : Set (ℕ → AddCircle (1 : ℝ))) := by
+  change IsClosed {x : ℕ → AddCircle (1 : ℝ) | ∀ n, 2 • x (n + 1) = x n}
+  simp only [Set.ofPred_forall]
+  exact isClosed_iInter fun n => isClosed_eq (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
+
+instance : CompactSpace DyadicSolenoid := closed_carrier.isClosedEmbedding_subtypeVal.compactSpace
+
+/-- The real flow has coordinate `t / 2^n` modulo one. -/
+def realFlow : ℝ →+ DyadicSolenoid where
+  toFun t := ⟨fun n => ((t / (2 : ℝ)^n : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)), by
+    intro n
+    rw [← AddCircle.coe_nsmul]
+    congr 1
+    rw [nsmul_eq_mul, pow_succ]
+    field_simp
+    ring⟩
+  map_zero' := by ext n; simp
+  map_add' s t := by ext n; simp [add_div]
+
+private theorem continuous_flow : Continuous realFlow := by
+  apply continuous_induced_rng.mpr
+  exact continuous_pi fun n => (AddCircle.continuous_mk' (1 : ℝ)).comp
+    (continuous_id.div_const ((2 : ℝ)^n))
+
+private theorem coordinates (x : DyadicSolenoid) (n k : ℕ) :
+    (2 ^ k : ℕ) • x.1 (n + k) = x.1 n := by
+  induction k with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ k ih =>
+    rw [pow_succ, mul_smul, show n + (k + 1) = (n + k) + 1 by omega,
+      x.2 (n + k)]
+    exact ih
+
+private theorem finite_match (x : DyadicSolenoid) (s : Finset ℕ) :
+    ∃ t : ℝ, ∀ n ∈ s, (realFlow t).1 n = x.1 n := by
+  let N := s.sup id
+  obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := QuotientAddGroup.mk'_surjective (AddSubgroup.zmultiples (1 : ℝ)) (x.1 N)
+  change (r : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) = x.1 N at hr
+  refine ⟨(2 : ℝ)^N * r, ?_⟩
+  intro n hn
+  have hnN : n ≤ N := Finset.le_sup (f := id) hn
+  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hnN
+  have heq : (realFlow ((2 : ℝ)^N * r)).1 n = (2 ^ k : ℕ) • (r : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) := by
+    change (((2 : ℝ)^N * r / 2^n : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ)) = _
+    rw [← AddCircle.coe_nsmul]
+    congr 1
+    rw [nsmul_eq_mul, hk, pow_add]
+    push_cast
+    field_simp
+  rw [heq, hr, hk]
+  exact coordinates x n k
+
+private theorem dense_flow : DenseRange realFlow := by
+  rw [DenseRange]
+  intro x
+  rw [mem_closure_iff_nhds']
+  intro neighborhood hn
+  change neighborhood ∈ @nhds DyadicSolenoid
+    (TopologicalSpace.induced Subtype.val
+      (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace (ℕ → AddCircle (1 : ℝ)))) x at hn
+  rw [mem_nhds_induced] at hn
+  obtain ⟨ambient, ha, hsub⟩ := hn
+  classical
+  simp only [nhds_pi, Filter.mem_pi'] at ha
+  obtain ⟨indices, coordinateSets, hx, hc⟩ := ha
+  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := finite_match x indices
+  refine ⟨⟨realFlow t, ⟨t, rfl⟩⟩, hsub ?_⟩
+  apply hc
+  intro n hn
+  rw [ht n hn]
+  exact mem_of_mem_nhds (hx n)
+
+instance : PreconnectedSpace DyadicSolenoid :=
+  DenseRange.preconnectedSpace dense_flow continuous_flow
+
+instance : ConnectedSpace DyadicSolenoid := ⟨⟨0⟩⟩
+
+private theorem multiply_surjective (m : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) :
+    Function.Surjective (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => m • x) := by
+  have hclosed : IsClosed (Set.range (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => m • x)) :=
+    (isCompact_range (continuous_id.nsmul m)).isClosed
+  have hsub : Set.range realFlow ⊆ Set.range (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => m • x) := by
+    rintro _ ⟨t, rfl⟩
+    refine ⟨realFlow (t / m), ?_⟩
+    change m • realFlow (t / m) = realFlow t
+    rw [← map_nsmul, nsmul_eq_mul, mul_div_cancel₀ _ (by exact_mod_cast hm.ne')]
+  intro x
+  exact (closure_minimal hsub hclosed) (dense_flow x)
+
+private theorem no_two_torsion (x : DyadicSolenoid) (hx : 2 • x = 0) : x = 0 := by
+  ext n
+  have he := congrArg (fun y : DyadicSolenoid => y.1 (n + 1)) hx
+  change 2 • x.1 (n + 1) = 0 at he
+  rw [x.2 n] at he
+  exact he
+
+private def third : AddCircle (1 : ℝ) := ((1 / 3 : ℝ) : AddCircle (1 : ℝ))
+
+private theorem third_three : 3 • third = 0 := by
+  rw [third, ← AddCircle.coe_nsmul, nsmul_eq_mul]
+  norm_num
+
+private theorem third_two : 2 • third = -third := by
+  apply eq_neg_iff_add_eq_zero.mpr
+  simpa only [show 3 = 2 + 1 from rfl, add_nsmul, one_nsmul] using third_three
+
+/-- The nonzero alternating order-three point, with coordinate `(-1)^n / 3` modulo one. -/
+def thirdPoint : DyadicSolenoid :=
+  ⟨fun n => ((-1 : ℤ)^n) • third, by
+    intro n
+    simp only [pow_succ, mul_smul, neg_one_zsmul, smul_neg]
+    rw [smul_comm, third_two, smul_neg, neg_neg]⟩
+
+private theorem point_nonzero : thirdPoint ≠ 0 := by
+  intro h
+  have he := congrArg (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => x.1 0) h
+  have ht : third = 0 := by simpa [thirdPoint] using he
+  have hmem : (1 / 3 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 := by constructor <;> norm_num
+  have := (AddCircle.coe_eq_zero_iff_of_mem_Ico hmem).mp ht
+  norm_num at this
+
+private theorem point_three : 3 • thirdPoint = 0 := by
+  ext n
+  change 3 • (((-1 : ℤ)^n) • third) = 0
+  rw [smul_comm, third_three, smul_zero]
+
+private theorem algebraic_time : ∃ phi : ℚ →+ DyadicSolenoid, phi 1 = thirdPoint := by
+  let : DivisibleBy DyadicSolenoid ℕ :=
+    divisibleByOfSMulRightSurj DyadicSolenoid ℕ
+      (fun {n} hn => multiply_surjective n (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero hn))
+  let : DivisibleBy DyadicSolenoid ℤ := AddGroup.divisibleByIntOfDivisibleByNat _
+  obtain ⟨phi, hp⟩ := (Module.Baer.of_divisible DyadicSolenoid).extension_property_addMonoidHom
+    (Int.castAddHom ℚ) (by intro a b h; exact Int.cast_injective h)
+    (zmultiplesHom DyadicSolenoid thirdPoint)
+  refine ⟨phi, ?_⟩
+  have := DFunLike.congr_fun hp (1 : ℤ)
+  simpa using this
+
+private theorem quarter_sequence (phi : ℚ →+ DyadicSolenoid) (hp : phi 1 = thirdPoint) :
+    ∀ n : ℕ, phi ((1 / 4 : ℚ)^n) = thirdPoint := by
+  have hinj2 : Function.Injective (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => 2 • x) := by
+    intro x y he
+    change 2 • x = 2 • y at he
+    have hz : 2 • (x - y) = 0 := by rw [smul_sub, he, sub_self]
+    exact sub_eq_zero.mp (no_two_torsion _ hz)
+  have hinj4 : Function.Injective (fun x : DyadicSolenoid => 4 • x) := by
+    intro x y he
+    apply hinj2
+    apply hinj2
+    simpa only [← mul_smul, show (2 : ℕ) * 2 = 4 from rfl] using he
+  have hfour : 4 • thirdPoint = thirdPoint := by
+    simp only [show 4 = 3 + 1 from rfl, add_nsmul, one_nsmul, point_three, zero_add]
+  intro n
+  induction n with

+  | succ n ih =>
